title: Railway Safety & Human Factors

canonicalTerminology.definition: A hazard is a condition or source with the potential to cause harm or contribute to an unwanted event.

claims.text: Railway safety management combines technical controls, organisational arrangements and human performance considerations across the system lifecycle.
claims.applicabilityNote: Educational canonical statement. Apply current controlled legislation, standards and organisational safety procedures where operational decisions are involved.

visualSpecs.purpose: Show defence-in-depth across technical, procedural and human or organisational layers.

prohibitedUnsupportedClaims: Do not invent risk acceptance thresholds, safe limits or operating rules.
Do not present classroom hazard analysis as an approved safety case or operational instruction.
